events.text: You stand on the edge of your own sky and look across at the domains of the other gods: fields of weather and fire and dreaming, each with a god sitting on it like a hen. None of them earned what they hold. They only came first. Behind you, your own host waits for a word, and the stars nearest you have already begun to dim.

choices.text: Give the word

effects.log: Your host pours out across the dark like a river finding its old bed. The gods begin to count their doors.

choices.text: Raise your hand, and wait one breath longer

effects.log: You let them wait. Then you lower your hand, and the sky is never the same again.

choices.text: Burn your old pantheon seal in front of them

effects.log: The seal curls up in the light. Nobody in your host will ever kneel to anyone else.

events.text: On the highest terrace of your palace there is a stone where nobody sits. You have it swept, and set a cup of tea beside it, and send heralds down every golden road with one sentence: whoever can climb this high may ask the Dao a question, and it will be answered. The heralds look at each other. The gods have never answered anything.

choices.text: Sit on the stone yourself

effects.log: You sit and wait. The tea grows cold. On the third day the first immortal arrives, out of breath.

choices.text: Leave the stone empty

effects.log: You stand beside it instead. Whoever comes will have to decide who the stone is for.

choices.text: Write the first question yourself

effects.log: You carve it into the stone: what is the Dao for? Nobody has answered it yet, including you.

events.text: You set a chair in the empty space between the four pantheons, where no god has ever wanted to stand because it belongs to nobody. Four halls go quiet at once. A Grove elder sends a seed, a Storm herald a hailstone, a Hall envoy nothing at all, and the Will of Heaven a mirror. Each gift is a question: whose side are you on?

choices.text: Return all four gifts

effects.log: Each pantheon gets its gift back with the same note: none. The four halls are offended equally, which is the beginning of fairness.

choices.text: Keep all four on a single shelf

effects.log: They sit side by side, the seed and the hail and the mirror and the nothing. Visitors stare at them for centuries.

choices.text: Plant the seed, melt the hail, break the mirror

effects.log: The Grove is pleased, the Storm amused, the Sun furious. The Hall writes it down.

events.text: The herald of the god you threw down comes to your gate on foot, still in the colours of a domain that is no longer theirs. "My lord asks only," the herald says, "that the temple of the old dawn be left standing. Mortals pray there who do not know the god has changed."

choices.text: Leave the temple standing

effects.log: The temple stands. Its mortals pray to you now, and never know it.

choices.text: Burn it, so they learn

effects.log: The temple burns in a thousand worlds at once. They learn.

choices.text: Keep the herald as your own

effects.log: The herald stays, and wears your colours by spring. Heralds always know where the wind blows.

events.text: Your host drags the throne of the fallen god across your sky as a trophy. It is too big for any hall you have, so you leave it standing on an empty cloud, where the other gods can see it every morning.

choices.text: Sit on it once

effects.log: It is uncomfortable, as stolen thrones are. You sit on it long enough to be seen.

choices.text: Break it into steps for your stair

effects.log: Every god who climbs to you now climbs over the throne of another.

events.text: In the vaults of the domain you took, a god's child is hiding among the jars of starlight, holding a wooden sword that could not cut paper. The child points it at you and does not lower it, even when it starts to shake.

choices.text: Send the child after its parent

effects.log: You open the door of the vault and let the child walk out. The wooden sword stays pointed at you the whole way.

choices.text: Take the sword away

effects.log: You break the wooden sword across your knee. Somewhere a story about you begins, and it is not a kind one.

choices.text: Teach the child to hold it properly

effects.log: You adjust the grip. The child stares at you in confusion and then, slowly, in hatred. Good.

events.text: The islands of the immortals hang in a sea of cloud, each with its pavilions and its arrays and its elders who have never once been afraid. You come out of the sun, and the arrays go dark one by one, and the elders learn.

choices.text: Take the treasuries and go

effects.log: You take everything that shines and leave everything that breathes. The isles will remember the difference.

choices.text: Take the elders' seals too

effects.log: You take the seals of their sects. A hundred sects below the clouds wake without a name.

choices.text: Leave one island untouched

effects.log: One island is spared, and its elders never know why. They build a shrine to the mystery.

events.text: An old immortal of the islands kneels on the jade stair of her sect, alone, between your host and her disciples. "I was a guest at the Upper Realm's court when you were a Saint," she says. "You poured my tea. Remember that."

choices.text: Remember it, and pass by

effects.log: You pass her sect by. Her disciples will tell the story wrong, as if she frightened you.

choices.text: Pour her one more cup

effects.log: You pour her tea on the stair, and then you empty her sect's vaults. She drinks it anyway.

choices.text: Tell her you remember nothing

effects.log: Her face does not change. Behind her, a disciple begins, very quietly, to cry.

events.text: Your raid breaks against the domain like surf on a cliff. When you are carried home, your host does not meet your eyes, and the stars that dimmed for you have begun, a little, to shine again.

choices.text: Laugh it off

effects.log: You laugh, and your host laughs with you, too loudly. Next time, they will be afraid of losing too.

choices.text: Punish the captain who broke first

effects.log: The captain is cast off your sky. Your host learns that you lose badly.

choices.text: Study the god's guard all night

effects.log: By dawn you have found the gap in it. There will be a next time.

events.text: The Seven Swords of Jade Dawn come for you at the hour when the stars change watch: seven Righteous Immortals in white, their blades so bright that your own shadow hides behind you. The youngest, a sword-girl called Baek Yuhwa, is shaking, and holds her place anyway.

choices.text: Meet all seven in the open

effects.log: You step out into their light and let them see you.

choices.text: Strike the eldest first, from behind the light

effects.log: You come out of your own shadow at the eldest's back.

choices.text: Spare the youngest, whatever happens

effects.log: You decide before the first blade moves: Baek Yuhwa will walk away from this.

events.text: Guardian Cheolbyeok of the Southern Gate comes alone, in armour forged from the gate itself, and plants his spear at the border of your sky. Behind him, far back on the road, a sword in white: Baek Yuhwa, older now, has come to watch how you fight.

choices.text: Fight the Guardian where he stands

effects.log: You walk to the border and meet the gate of heaven with your hands.

choices.text: Let him walk into your sky first

effects.log: You let the Guardian cross the border. Your sky closes behind him like a mouth.

choices.text: Tell Baek Yuhwa to go home

effects.log: You call across the road to her. She does not answer. She does not leave, either.

events.text: The twins Ha-eun and Ha-ram of the Silent Hall do not come at all: they are simply there one morning, at the foot of your bed, one holding a knife of moonlight and the other a knife of no light at all. Baek Yuhwa is with them, and this time her sword is drawn.

choices.text: Rise and face them

effects.log: You rise slowly, the way a mountain would if it could.

choices.text: Pretend to sleep a moment longer

effects.log: You keep your eyes closed until the knives are close enough to catch.

choices.text: Turn your back on Baek Yuhwa

effects.log: You put your back to her, on purpose. Whatever she does with it will be her choice.

events.text: The Thousand-Year Monk Wonhyo-seon climbs your stair on his knees, one step at a time, chanting. Every step he climbs, one of your stars goes out. He has been climbing for a year. He reaches the top this morning.

choices.text: Meet him at the top of the stair

effects.log: You stand at the top of your own stair and wait for the last chant.

choices.text: Break the stair under him

effects.log: You break the stair. The monk keeps climbing, on nothing, still chanting.

events.text: Lady Seomun of the Nine Clouds brings an army of Righteous Immortals and the war-banners of every sect you emptied. At her side rides Baek Yuhwa, a captain now, her white robes grey with the dust of your roads. She has a scar from the night of the twins. It is the shape of your hand.

choices.text: Break the army on your own

effects.log: You go out to meet the army of the Nine Clouds alone.

choices.text: Let them besiege an empty palace

effects.log: You leave your palace empty and fall on their camp from the dark.

events.text: Cheonbeol, the Executioner of Heaven, has no face: only a hood, and under it a blade that has ended a god once in every age. Behind the Executioner the whole sky is white with Righteous Immortals. This is the last wave. Heaven has nothing left to send after it, and you have nothing left to lose but everything.

choices.text: Walk out to the Executioner

effects.log: You walk out under a white sky. Nobody on either side breathes.

choices.text: Strike before the hood lifts

effects.log: You move before the Executioner does, which nobody has ever done.

events.text: Cheonbeol, the Executioner of Heaven, has no face: only a hood, and under it a blade that has ended a god once in every age. Behind the Executioner the sky is white with Righteous Immortals, and at their front rides Baek Yuhwa, the sword-girl you spared on the first night. She looks at you for a long time, and then at the Executioner.

choices.text: Walk out to the Executioner

effects.log: You walk out under a white sky. Nobody on either side breathes.

choices.text: Strike before the hood lifts

effects.log: You move before the Executioner does, which nobody has ever done.

choices.text: Look at Baek Yuhwa, and wait

effects.log: You only look at her. Baek Yuhwa lowers her sword, and turns her horse, and half of the white sky turns with her.

events.text: Yeon Seorin has stood at the same gate of the Dao for nine thousand years. She climbs to the terraces of your conference with the face of someone who has stopped hoping and come anyway, and asks you what she is doing wrong.

choices.text: Tell her she is doing nothing wrong

effects.log: Yeon Seorin weeps, and then laughs. A gate nine thousand years shut opens a finger's width.

choices.text: Tell her she is standing at the wrong gate

effects.log: She stares at you for a full day. Then she turns around, and there is another gate behind her.

choices.text: Ask her what she would tell a student

effects.log: She begins to answer, and stops, and her face changes. She has heard herself.

events.text: Gwak Taeseong, a Sword Immortal of a thousand duels, stands up in the middle of your first lecture and says, loud enough for every terrace: "The Dao is not taught. It is taken. I came to see a god admit it."

choices.text: Admit that some of it is taken

effects.log: You agree with half of what he said. He has no idea what to do with that, and sits down, scowling, to listen.

choices.text: Take his sword from him, gently

effects.log: You take it without moving, and give it back. "Like that?" you ask. He leaves the terraces and swears to come back.

choices.text: Invite him to give the next lecture

effects.log: Gwak Taeseong gives it. It is not bad. Afterwards he asks, roughly, if you will hear his questions.

events.text: Gwak Taeseong is back, older and leaner, and this time he does not interrupt. He waits until the last immortal has asked the last question, and then he asks his: "Why did you give my sword back?"

choices.text: "Because it was yours."

effects.log: He is silent for a long time. Then he bows, the full bow, to the ground. The rivalry is over.

choices.text: "Because I did not need it."

effects.log: He nods, slowly, as if you had struck him. He will be back again.

events.text: Gwak Taeseong runs the sword terraces of your conference now, as fierce as ever. His students are terrified of him and would die for him. He brings you the best of them, a mortal-born boy called Ha Jiwoo who fishes for stars.

choices.text: Hear the boy's question

effects.log: Ha Jiwoo asks why the stars bite. Nobody has ever asked you anything so good.

choices.text: Tell Gwak he has become a teacher

effects.log: Gwak Taeseong looks appalled, and then, when he thinks you cannot see, very proud.

events.text: A hundred immortals bring you the same question in a hundred forms: how can the Dao be one, if every one of us walks a different road? They have been arguing about it on the lower terraces for a month, loudly.

choices.text: Tell them every road is the road

effects.log: The terraces go quiet. It is too simple to be true, which is why it takes them a century to believe it.

choices.text: Tell them to stop arguing and walk

effects.log: They walk. Some of them, for the first time in ten thousand years, actually move.

choices.text: Ask them to count the roads

effects.log: They begin to count. They never finish. Several of them reach the next realm trying.

events.text: An immortal who sold her sect to the Calamity of an earlier age comes to the conference hooded, hoping nobody will know her. Everybody knows her. She asks, in a whisper, whether a road walked wrongly can be walked again.

choices.text: Tell her yes, and seat her in front

effects.log: You give her the front row. The terraces mutter for a season and then forget to.

choices.text: Tell her the road remembers

effects.log: She nods. She knew. She came to hear someone say it who would not lie.

choices.text: Ask the others whether they would forgive her

effects.log: The terraces argue for a year. It is the best lesson of the conference.

events.text: The conference's last day: the immortals have gone quiet, the tea is cold, and a child of one of the gods has climbed onto the empty stone of the first question and fallen asleep there. Nobody dares to wake her.

choices.text: Let her sleep, and end the conference in whispers

effects.log: You end the conference in whispers. It is the one every immortal remembers best.

choices.text: Wake her, and ask her the first question

effects.log: She thinks about it with her whole face, and says: "To play in." The terraces will argue about it for an age.

events.text: A sect master from below the clouds has climbed all the way to your conference on foot, with a basket of rice cakes for the gods, and now stands at the edge of the terraces too frightened of the immortals to step onto them.

choices.text: Walk out and take a rice cake

effects.log: You eat a rice cake in front of ten thousand immortals. The sect master is famous below for ever.

choices.text: Make the immortals come to the sect master

effects.log: Ten thousand immortals file past to take a rice cake each. None of them say a word about it.

events.text: The light you turned on your old sect below falls on its mountain at dawn. Below, the youngest disciples run out of their dormitories in their sleeping robes, and the old elders stand in the courtyard and do not try to explain it.

choices.text: Let them see your shape in the light

effects.log: For a moment, a hooded figure stands in the sun over the sect. It is painted on the main hall within the year.

choices.text: Stay hidden in it

effects.log: The light is only light. The disciples decide it was the mountain itself, which is nearly true.

events.text: In the margin of the Book of Fates, beside a line that has not happened yet, you write a small mark in your own hand. A clerk of the Heavenly Court sees it, turns white, and quietly closes the book.

choices.text: Tell the clerk it is a gift

effects.log: The clerk nods very fast. Nobody will touch that margin for as long as heaven lasts.

choices.text: Tell the clerk nothing

effects.log: The clerk tells nobody. The clerk will dream about your handwriting for a thousand years.

events.text: Your disciple feels it in the middle of a meal: a hand of light on the crown of the head, and a realm opening like a door kicked from the other side. The bowl breaks. Every disciple at the table stands up at once.

choices.text: Speak one word to your disciple

effects.log: You say: "Walk." Your disciple, for the rest of a long life, will.

choices.text: Say nothing

effects.log: Your disciple looks up at the sky for a very long time, and bows to it.

events.text: Two pantheons are at war, and the first stars between them have gone out. Envoys from both sides arrive at your chair on the same morning, each with a list of the other's crimes. Both lists are true.

choices.text: Read both lists aloud, side by side

effects.log: The envoys listen to each other's crimes in your voice. Neither of them enjoys it.

choices.text: Send both envoys home unheard

effects.log: They go home insulted. The war goes on, but both sides now know someone is watching.

events.text: A god has begun selling the domain they hold: rain to the highest bidder, harvests to whichever kingdom builds the tallest temple. Below the clouds, a river has stopped in the middle of a valley because nobody paid for it.

choices.text: Go down and look at the river

effects.log: You stand on the dry riverbed among the mortals. Nobody knows who you are. Everybody knows the river is wrong.

choices.text: Summon the god's accounts

effects.log: The accounts arrive in a cart drawn by eight oxen. You read every page.

events.text: Hyeolsa the Red Comet was a god once, of a domain nobody remembers now. Cast out of every pantheon, it has become a Calamity Star of its own, and it is raiding the edges of heaven the way a fox raids a henhouse: one at a time, and laughing.

choices.text: Watch where it strikes next

effects.log: You watch for a year. Hyeolsa never strikes the same domain twice, and always on a festival.

choices.text: Send it a single question

effects.log: You ask Hyeolsa what it wants. The answer comes back, written in fire: "To be counted."

events.text: One pantheon has taken so many domains that its hall now stands over half of heaven, and the other three meet in secret, in dreams and in weather, to decide what to do about it. Each of them invites you.

choices.text: Go to none of the secret meetings

effects.log: You stay in your chair, in the open. The three pantheons are furious, and a little ashamed.

choices.text: Go to all of them, openly

effects.log: You walk into each secret meeting by the front door. They stop being secret.

events.text: Your decree is copied by ten thousand clerks and carried down every golden road, and every god who reads it stops what they are doing for the length of one breath. Heaven has a law again, and it has your handwriting.

choices.text: Read it aloud once more, to yourself

effects.log: You read it in the empty hall. It sounds, even to you, like the weather.

choices.text: Burn your draft

effects.log: The draft burns. Only the decree remains, which is how it should be.

events.text: Your decree comes back to you unopened, in a hundred envelopes, from a hundred halls. The gods have not refused it. They have simply decided not to have received it.

choices.text: Write it again, more plainly

effects.log: You write it in fewer words. You will need it to be heard next time.

choices.text: Keep one envelope as a reminder

effects.log: You keep the envelope from the hall that sent it back first. You will remember that hall.

events.text: The two champions kneel in the empty hall, one on each side of your chair, and neither will look at the other. When they leave, they leave by the same door, which has not happened since the beginning of the clash.

choices.text: Watch them go

effects.log: They walk out side by side and do not speak. It is, you think, a start.

choices.text: Call after them: "Again in a thousand years."

effects.log: Both champions stop, and turn, and, to everyone's astonishment, laugh.

events.text: One champion kneels to your judgement. The other leaves the hall with your blood on their sword, and a look on their face as if they had expected to feel better. The clash goes on, quieter.

choices.text: Bind the wound and go back to your chair

effects.log: You sit again. The scales of heaven tilt, and then, slowly, begin to steady.

choices.text: Send the kneeling one after the other

effects.log: The kneeling champion follows the other out. Perhaps they will talk.

events.text: Both champions stand over you when the trial is done, and for a moment heaven holds its breath to see whether the Arbiter will rise again. You rise. It takes a long time. Both of them watch it all the way.

choices.text: Thank them both

effects.log: You thank them for the trial, with blood in your mouth. They do not know what to make of it.

choices.text: Promise them a second trial

effects.log: You promise them a second trial. They go home and train, both, for a hundred years.

events.text: You bend one law of heaven, only slightly, and in a thousand worlds a clock runs a breath slower or a war forgets itself. Nobody notices. That is how you know you did it right.

choices.text: Bend nothing else today

effects.log: You leave the rest of heaven's laws exactly where they are. It takes more strength than bending them.

choices.text: Write down what you changed

effects.log: You write it in the margin of the Book of Laws, so the next Arbiter will know.
